channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Eric Schmidt’s 1% Anthropic Stake Set to Pay Massive Windfall
item.description: Former Google Chief Executive Officer Eric Schmidt owns around 1% of Anthropic PBC thanks to his early investment in the startup, according to people familiar with the matter, setting him up for one of the largest individual windfalls from the company’s imminent public market debut.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Tom Maloney

item.title: JPMorgan's 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions
item.description: David Kelly, chief global strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, and Stephen Parker, co-head of global investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discuss their latest Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, which projects about 7% annual returns for 60/40 portfolios over the next 10–15 years. They speak on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FTC Requires Publicis to Offer Equal Access to LiveRamp Data
item.description: The US Federal Trade Commission said it will allow Publicis Groupe SA to complete the $2.2 billion acquisition of LiveRamp Holdings Inc. if the French media giant agrees to offer equal access to the digital advertising platform’s data connectivity services to rivals.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen

item.title: Intel Asks FCC to Allow Upgrades for Banned Foreign Robots
item.description: Intel Corp. asked the Federal Communications Commission to make an exception to a recent ban on foreign-made advanced robotics, telling the agency it needs continued access to “niche” equipment critical to US semiconductor manufacturing.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis and Ian King

item.title: Goldman's Lynam Isn't Worried About Access to Debt Amid AI Buildout
item.description: Amanda Lynam, chief credit strategist at Goldman Sachs, says recent widening in AI-related credit spreads resembles an earlier episode but differs because high-yield debt is now leading the move and investors are raising fundamental questions. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Launches Probe in First Sampling Mission to a Moon of Mars
item.description: Japan launched a probe bound for a moon of Mars, giving the nation a head start over China in the race to become the first to return samples from the Red Planet or one of its moons.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Takahashi

item.title: Nscale, Anthropic in Talks for $45 Billion Cloud Computing Deal
item.description: Nscale Ltd., the AI cloud computing firm, is in talks to sell computing power to Anthropic PBC in a deal that could be worth about $45 billion, according to people familiar with the negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz, Dina Bass and Brody Ford

item.title: AI Firm Nscale Faces Investor Pushback Over IPO Valuation
item.description: Bloomberg's Brody Ford said that issues facing the IPO of AI firm Nscale are 'endemic' to the larger AI data center industry as developers try to source power and labor and contend with potential delays. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz said that the tone has shifted for AI IPOs as more companies slow down on going public before the end of the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Merz Warns Europe That It’s Underestimating the Russian Threat
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that Europe has 'underestimated' the Russia's impact on the continent, saying 'Russia is on the way to destabilize the entire political order' of the region. Merz told Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua that many in Germany are not taking the threat seriously enough, warning that the Russia has larger aims than the current conflict. Merz said 'this is not only territorial gain in Ukraine. They fear democracy. They fear open societies. They fear the success of European integration.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: T.Rowe's Crypto ETF Outpaces S&P
item.description: Blue Macellari, head of digital assets at T.Rowe Price, joins Isabelle Lee and Eric Balchunas on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." They discuss T. Rowe Price Active Crypto ETF (ticker: TKNZ). The fund is outpacing the broader market since its launch in July. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hamilton Lane: AI’s Biggest Returns Have Been Private
item.description: Hamilton Lane Executive Co-Chairman Erik Hirsch says much of the wealth created by the AI boom has so far accrued in the private markets, as companies stay private longer and tap increasingly deep pools of capital. With exposure to OpenAI and Anthropic through its venture and growth relationships, Hirsch discusses how investors can access private AI companies through funds, secondaries and co-investments - and why even as some of AI’s biggest names head toward IPOs, going public is no longer the default path for most technology companies. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Already Developing Higher-End HomeView
item.description: Apple's new HomeView has been a long time coming - but now, Apple is already developing a higher-end version of the device with a robotic limb, which can automatically swivel the screen toward whoever is speaking. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman joins Ed Ludlow with the details from this week's Power On newsletter on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic, Musk Offer Competing Visions for Sharing AI Wealth
item.description: Anthropic plans to dedicate 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, offering its own approach to sharing the potential wealth created by AI as concerns grow about AI-driven labor disruption. Bloomberg’s Mike Shepard discusses how the plan differs from proposals for a government-run fund - and from Elon Musk’s pledge to give every child in America a share of SpaceX - as technology leaders confront a broader question: who should benefit financially from the AI boom? He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nscale’s $30B IPO Ambition Meets Investor Pushback
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow looks at why Nscale is facing pushback to its $30 billion IPO valuation target, with some investors suggesting $16 to $19 billion instead. Plus, Anthropic plans to put 5% of its shares into a new public benefit fund to address "the public good," and a former OpenAI software engineer charged with placing a recording device in one of the company's offices is set to appear in court today. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Germany's Merz Says Russia's Push to Destabilize Europe Is Underestimated
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned against complacency over the dangers posed by Russia, saying that President Vladimir Putin is seeking to not only defeat Ukraine, but to also undermine democracy in Europe and further integration. “My biggest concern is the underestimated Russian impact on our societies,” Merz said Monday in an exclusive interview with Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua. “Russia is on the way to destabilize the entire political order of our European continent.” Merz also said Europe has the ability to harness its strength and overcome economic malaise as he reinforced his plan to overhaul Germany’s social system and open it to investment in areas such as industrial artificial intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Bugging Office Stays Jailed for Now
item.description: The OpenAI software engineer charged with planting a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices must remain in jail for the time being, a federal judge ruled.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: US Moves to Bar China’s DeepSeek From Federal Agency Systems
item.description: The Trump administration barred civilian US government agencies from using products or services from Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek, citing a potential threat to national security from the company’s operations in China.
item.dc:creator: Michael Shepard

item.title: Tech Stocks Pull S&P 500 Higher as Opportunistic Buyers Step In
item.description: Chips companies rallied in Monday trading, helping stocks rebound after the worst week for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index since the tariff turmoil of April 2025.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: Vinted Cracks Down on Looted Goods After French Riots
item.description: Vinted, a secondhand online marketplace that counts France as one of its largest markets, has seen an influx of listings suspected to contain looted items after riots broke out across the country.
item.dc:creator: Yazhou Sun

item.title: Musk Plans to Gift SpaceX Shares to Kids Through Trump Accounts
item.description: Elon Musk vowed to distribute a share of SpaceX to each child in the US, a multibillion-dollar pledge that adds to a string of sizable donations from the tech industry for the benefit of the American public.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Ed Ludlow
